Case study: one tool for development

Real project · anonymised

    −27%fewer Polarion licences (800 → 580)
    ProblemTwo sync steps and a Polarion licence for every role+

    Features came from the client platform (DevStack) and were synced into Polarion first, then synced again into our project Jira, where the developers work. Two sync steps meant manual effort, delays and two places to check. Every role needed a Polarion licence.

    SolutionDirect plugin sync from DevStack – development fully in Jira+

    I designed a new requirements concept: a plugin syncs features directly from DevStack into our project Jira. Requirements, user stories and baselines now live in Jira. Polarion is only used for testing: test cases are synced, test runs and records stay there.

    Result−220 licences (800 → 580) and one tool for developers+

    Polarion licences dropped from about 800 to about 580 (−220, −27%) because only the test team still needs Polarion. On top of that: one sync instead of two, one tool for all developers and less manual effort.
